claude_seats.summary: I read the full .quorum-brief.md (1713 lines) and cross-checked every hunk against the live worktree. The diff implements exactly PVL-001 EV-11 for PMAT-4166: two new shrink-only ratchet gates (theorem-pairing / PV-RAT-001, depends-on-present / PV-RAT-002) in crates/aprender-contracts/src/lint/ratchet_gates.rs, wired into NAMED_GATES (5→7) and GateExtra (internally-tagged, backward-compatible), plus a repeatable `--gate` CLI flag with documented rank/meet semantics (refusal>reject>decline>pass) in crates/aprender-contracts-cli/src/commands/lint.rs. I traced run_gates()'s meet logic and all 7 new integration tests in tests/ev11_lint_ratchets.rs line-by-line against the source (including the SingleGateReport #[serde(flatten)] pattern that makes top-level JSON field assertions valid, and exit_code_for()'s fallthrough that gives UnknownGate exit 1) and found every exit code, stderr substring, and JSON shape the tests assert to be exactly what the code produces — no mismatches. I confirmed the new gates are NOT added to contracts/lint-baseline.json's `armed_gates` list (mirroring the existing unarmed `valid-under` gate), so this diff does not widen the default `pv lint` pass/fail surface — the two new gates only judge when explicitly named via `--gate`, matching the ticket's EV-11 probe. I empirically corroborated the theorem-pairing baseline (131 `.lean` theorem-module files measured directly via `find`, and a substring-based upper-bound pairing check found exactly 1 paired — matching the commit's claimed "131 modules, 1 paired" / baseline 130 exactly) and the depends-on-present baseline is well-reconciled: collect_yaml_files's directory exclusions (kaizen/legacy/pipelines/publish-manifests/quarantine, 49 yaml files measured) plus 4 named-file exclusions account for essentially the full 1884-vs-1830 gap, and the committed lint-baseline.json's independently-computed ONT-7 `contracts_without_valid_under: 386` and `ont.contracts_total: 1883` are consistent (within 1) with the depends-on-present commit's claimed 387 kernel contracts / 1830 checked — two gates walking the same corpus landing on nearly identical counts is strong cross-corroboration, not something a fabricated number would produce. I also confirmed make lint-ratchet is never invoked from any .github/workflows/*.yml (grep, no matches), the new CI test-command file (456-…) uses a free ordinal between 450 and 455 per CLAUDE.md's rule, all Σ glyphs used in the new contract's formal fields are declared in contracts/ontology.yaml, and commit 1c28b4c38's removal of a redundant `&& !contract.is_registry()` check is provably safe because Contract::kind() already folds registry:true kernels into Registry. No file was modified during this review. Across all of this I found zero contradictions, zero weakened gates, and zero unbacked receipt claims, so the verdict is PASS.

Reviewed PMAT-4166 (PVL-001 EV-11) implementation of two shrink-only `pv lint` ratchets. Verified: (1) repeatable `--gate` flag with Vec<String> type supports multiple invocations; (2) `run_gates()` computes meet correctly via rank function (pass < decline < reject < refusal); (3) gate implementations in ratchet_gates.rs contain zero writes to contracts/lint-baseline.json; (4) lint_ratchet.sh (the sole writer) refuses rises and only lowers baselines; (5) theorem-pairing pairing rule enforces full dotted module name on identifier boundaries; (6) depends-on-present counts only kernel-kind contracts via kind() method; (7) all six falsification tests (FALSIFY-RAT-001 through 006) are implemented; (8) real corpus probe passes and leaves baseline byte-identical; (9) integration with ontology R-8 (computed in every run) present in run_lint() loop; (10) gate count updated from 13 to 15; (11) baseline file structure preserves three new top-level keys across ont-ratchet --write. No refuting findings: no test asserts opposite of ticket, no gates weakened, no unsubstantiated claims.
